newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OMV 9 month profit flat, aims for record full-year.
newsitem.headline: OMV 9 month profit flat, aims for record full-year.

text.p: Austrian oil group OMV AG on Tuesday reported a flat 1.63 billion schillings ($154.2 million) net profit in the first nine months, despite a big drop in refining income, and said it was on track to better 1995's record earnings.
Group earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) rose nine percent to 2.21 billion schillings and pre-tax profit climbed 17 percent to 2.24 billion -- at the upper end of analysts' expectations.
"OMV expects the operating result for the full year to be higher than 1995," the firm said in a statement.
Last year OMV posted EBIT of 2.19 billion schillings and net profit of 1.73 billion.
Earnings rose in all sectors in the first nine months with the exception of plastics and refining, both of which suffered from low plastics prices.
Refining EBIT tumbled to 23 million schillings from 474 million on sales of 29.9 billion, up from 27.4 billion.
"This significant deterioration is due to lower petrochemicals prices and narrow refining margins," OMV said.

It also noted that a change in the way it valued oil product stocks and crude purchases had weighed on earnings by some 320 million schillings. OMV has introduced the internationally accepted last-in, first-out (LIFO) method.
Plastics EBIT slipped to 517 million schillings from 595 million on sales of 6.81 billion, down from 6.91 billion.
A turnaround in exploration & production and marketing, seen in the first six months, gathered pace in the third quarter.

OMV posted a 60 million schillings EBIT in exploration and production after a 300 million schillings loss in the year-ago period. Sales rose to four billion schillings from 3.84 billion. It traced the improvement to crude oil prices that recently touched post-Gulf War highs.
Marketing reported a 165 million schillings EBIT, compared with a 60 million schillings loss the previous year. Sales rose to 14.25 billion schillings from 12.18 billion.
OMV said it had reduced the number of its domestic service stations to 774 on September 30, from 822 in 1995, while it expanded its foreign network to 324 stations from 268.
Gas, the powerhouse of OMV's earnings, posted a steady 1.29 billion schillings EBIT on sales of 8.26 billion, up from 7.93 billion.
-- Janet McBride, Vienna Newsroom 43-1-531 12 254 ($ = 10.57 Austrian Schillings)
